title: Sam Parr on copywriting: hooks, slippery slope, long copy and copy work
summary: Sam Parr breaks down the copywriting frameworks he used at The Hustle and Hampton: punchy first lines, the curiosity gap, stories with the customer as hero, and short sentences. He also explains why long copy beats short if it's interesting, and how copy work builds taste.

principles.text: Each sentence only exists to get the next one read; the first line must punch.
principles.quote: the purpose of the first sentence is to get you read the second sentence and the purpose of the second sentence is to get you to read the third sentence and so on.

principles.text: Long copy converts better than short as long as it's interesting; boring is the real problem.
principles.quote: long will almost always convert better. Ugly will almost always convert better, but it just has to be interesting.

principles.text: Use stories to sell; there is no too long, only too boring.
principles.quote: There's no such thing as too long, just too boring.

principles.text: Make the customer the hero and your brand the guide.
principles.quote: a good brand positions themselves as the guide and the hero of the story is your customer.

principles.text: Write simply: one point per sentence, swap commas for periods, seventh-grade reading level.
principles.quote: usually when you need to have a comma, use a period. Short sentences uh are the best.

principles.text: Build taste by copying great work by hand for months until you learn its rules.
principles.quote: that's the number one thing to do is just to blindly copy until you find the rules of the language that you're trying to speak.
